concepts.learning_objective: Describe the position of an object using a reference point, distance and direction, and decide whether it is at rest or in motion.
Distinguish between total distance travelled and displacement for motion in a straight line.
Calculate average speed as total distance travelled divided by the time interval.
Calculate average velocity as displacement divided by the time interval and state its direction.
Distinguish between uniform and non-uniform motion in a straight line.
Calculate average acceleration as the change in velocity divided by the time interval.
Relate the direction of acceleration to whether the magnitude of velocity is increasing or decreasing.
Recognise that an object falling freely has a constant acceleration of about 9.8 m/s squared.
Plot a position-time graph from a data table by choosing axes and suitable scales.
Interpret the shape of a position-time graph to identify rest, constant velocity or changing velocity.
Calculate the magnitude of velocity from the slope of a straight-line position-time graph.
Interpret the slope of a velocity-time graph as acceleration and calculate it.
Calculate displacement from the area enclosed by a velocity-time graph and the time axis.
State the kinematic equations v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at squared and v squared = u squared + 2as and the condition for their use.
Apply the kinematic equations to find velocity, displacement, acceleration or time.
Explain how the stopping distance of a vehicle depends on its initial velocity and braking.

topics.title: Motion in a plane and uniform circular motion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify examples of motion in two dimensions.
Explain why uniform circular motion is accelerated even though the speed is constant.
Calculate distance, displacement and average speed for motion along a circle.
